summary.oneLiner: India's largest wine company, commanding over 60% of the domestic Elite & Premium wine market, with a diversified own-brands wine portfolio and a growing wine tourism business (vineyards, resorts and tasting rooms).
summary.business: Sula Vineyards produces and sells wine across Economy & Popular, Sula Classics and Elite & Premium (RASA, The Source, Dindori, Sula) price tiers under 50+ labels, distributed through distributors, licensed retail, HORECA, modern trade, e-commerce and the Canteen Stores Department to consumers across India and select export markets. currentContext.strategies: Continue to scale up nationwide distribution of The Source range further in FY27, building on the strategy of expanding its availability that paid off in FY26|Continue the cost rationalization program into FY27 after operating expenses (including S&D) declined 2% YoY in FY26|Invest most of capex over the next 3 years in expanding the wine tourism business, with a medium-term target to significantly expand the resort portfolio and room capacity|Reduce wine inventory carryover and working capital consumption by shifting grape procurement mix toward wine grapes and away from open-market table grapes|Advance sustainability agenda: shift focus from adding solar panels to adding battery energy storage systems for resilience against rising fuel and power costs|Expand international presence, marked by entry into Dubai as a step toward building Sula's presence in an international, lifestyle-driven market|Pursue targeted regional market expansion (e.g. Indore and other emerging regions) with region-specific engagement approaches|Strengthen on-trade footprint through tie-ups with hospitality/F&B partners and expanded presence across marquee outlets
currentContext.expansion: In FY26, Sula commissioned a new 1 million litre low-cost cellar at its Domaine Dindori unit (Maharashtra), built at 33% lower capex, dedicated to Economy & Popular brands, taking total winery capacity to 19.2 million litres. It also increased bottling capacity at two Maharashtra units (Nashik Winery and ND Wines facility), raising WIPS capture to ~100% in FY26 from ~85% in FY25. On the wine-tourism side, the company launched its 3rd resort, The Haven by Sula (50 keys, near York) in Q3 FY26, taking total room capacity to 154 keys, and commissioned a new tasting room and restaurant expansion at Domaine Sula (near Bengaluru) in January 2026. Management's stated Growth Strategy (FY26-FY29) targets accelerating earnings growth via six pillars: product development (new wine launches), sufficient capacity for growth, expanding market penetration (wider national availability of The Source and RASA, new defence listings, new markets), expanding wine tourism & D2C business, augmenting brand visibility, and strategic M&A. The company has signed a binding agreement to acquire Chandon's 19-acre wine estate in Dindori, Nashik, to expand its wine tourism footprint, with the transaction underway and further details to be shared on completion; it also intends to pursue further strategic investments and acquisitions in wine tourism and the Indian AlcoBev industry. On the ESG side, the company doubled its Battery Energy Storage System capacity to ~2,217 kW (~2 MW) and increased solar-powered irrigation pump capacity by 130 HP to a total of 253 HP, alongside continued solar PV capacity build-out (4,703 kWH installed) at its Maharashtra and Karnataka facilities.

risks.note: FY26 revenue and profitability were materially impacted by transient disruptions confined to a small number of states — a route-to-market disruption in Telangana (the company's third-largest market) during H1 and one-time tactical destocking in Karnataka (its second-largest market) in Q3 — showing exposure to state-level, single-market shocks.

A 3.7% YoY revenue decline in FY26 (to Rs. 596.2 crore) produced a much larger 30.6% decline in Operating EBITDA and 672 bps of margin contraction (24.07% to 17.35%), with PAT falling 63.5%, indicating profitability is highly sensitive to relatively small swings in sales volume.

FY25 included a one-time WIPS unwinding gain of Rs. 10.4 crore that created a high base effect depressing FY26 YoY comparisons, illustrating how non-recurring items can materially skew reported growth and margins in a given year.

risks.risk: Execution risk on pending wine-tourism acquisition
risks.note: The agreement to acquire Chandon's 19-acre wine estate in Dindori is described as 'currently underway' with details to be shared 'upon transaction completion' — an unclosed M&A commitment with no disclosed timeline or completion certainty.

Room capacity was expanded ~50% to 154 keys with the launch of The Haven by Sula; sustaining ~77% occupancy while continuing to add rooms is necessary to convert the added capacity into proportionate revenue growth.

Grape supply for winemaking depends on the annual harvest's quality and volume (Harvest 2026 was described as the sixth consecutive favourable vintage), exposing the business to weather and agri-climate variability inherent to viticulture.

Net Debt/EBITDA was reported below 3x (debt of Rs. 294 crore as of 31 March 2026), but FY26 EBITDA declined 30.6% YoY, meaning a further profitability decline would push leverage multiples higher from an already-reduced EBITDA base.

one-line thesis: Sula returned to top-line growth in Q4 (+7% YoY) driven by Wine Tourism (+17%) and elite brand recovery, though margins compressed due to a strategic shift to costlier wine grapes and a prior-year one-off gain. The strategic pivot toward high-margin hospitality (targeting >20% revenue mix) and the pending Chandon estate acquisition signal a structural re-rating from a pure-play winemaker to an integrated experiential luxury operator.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 142cr (+7% YoY); Full Year: INR 596cr (-2% ex-one-off). EBITDA: Flat absolute YoY (margins pressured by ~500bps from grape mix & prior year INR 3.5cr Karnataka pricing gain). PAT: -34% YoY (base effect of deferred tax credit in Q4FY25). Order Book: N/A (FMCG). Net Debt: ~INR 280cr (down from INR 285cr); Debt/EBITDA <3x. One-offs: Prior year Q4 had INR 3.5cr inventory pricing gain; Current year grape mix shift added 350-400bps cost pressure.
guidance: Revenue: Momentum carrying into FY27 (4 months straight growth); Wine Tourism to grow double-digits as 'The Haven' scales. Margins: Expect improvement post-Q3FY27 as grape mix impact normalizes; Opex controls ongoing. Order Inflow: N/A. Capex: FY27 regular capex < FY26 (INR 25cr); Heavy skew toward Tourism (3x winery capex); Chandon acquisition closing H1FY27.
order book & pipeline: N/A - FMCG inventory model. Channel inventory destocked in Q4 vs prior quarters. WIPS receivables at INR 81cr (controlled).
segment / subsidiary detail: Own Brands: +5% YoY in Q4; Elite/Premium mix at 79% of sales. The Source range +35% in Q4, now >10% of own brands. Wine Tourism: +17% revenue in Q4, +20% full year; Crossed INR 100cr annual run-rate (INR 110cr incl. wine sold onsite). Footfalls >4 lakh. Occupancy >70% (core resorts >80%).
growth verticals / optionality: Chandon Estate (19 acres) acquisition pending; Targeting >200 room keys within 1.5 years (vs current 154). New event pavilion (Q3FY27) and amphitheater expansion (Q2FY27). CSD listings expanding from 9 to 14 wines by Q4FY27. Potential entry into spirits/tequila via M&A (no target yet).
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin pressured by 350-400bps (expensive wine grapes used in economy labels due to surplus) + 150bps (prior year one-off). Packing material costs rising (West Asia conflict); Price hikes of 2-3% planned in free-pricing states. Opex reduced 3% YoY via cost controls.
capex / expansion: FY26: INR 25cr. FY27 Outlook: Lower regular capex than FY26 excluding Chandon deal. Allocation: ~75%+ toward Wine Tourism expansion (new resorts, pavilion, amphitheater).
capital allocation: Deleveraging priority (Net debt down to INR 280cr). Final dividend INR 2/share declared. M&A focused on tourism assets (Chandon) and potential craft spirit brands. No buyback mentioned.
risks & watch-items: Grape mix cost overhang persisting until next harvest (Q3FY27). EU FTA duty reduction (1 year out) threatening premium segment pricing power. Summer heat damaging retail inventory (lack of AC in trade). Unsustainable discounting by competitors in economy segment.
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic. Acknowledges margin pain as temporary/structural shift for quality. Aggressive on Tourism scaling ('laser focused'). Disciplined on M&A (waiting for right fit in spirits). Transparent on cost headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'margin compression' is partly a quality upgrade story (using premium grapes in entry-level wines) which may boost long-term brand equity despite short-term P&L hit. Tourism revenue reported ex-wine sales in P&L, understating the true INR 110cr scale of the vertical. 75% renewable energy mix achieved; moving to battery storage to hedge power costs.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grape surplus forcing use of premium grapes in economy wines; margin pressure | Indian Wine Consumers | beneficiary | High | Getting higher quality wine (Chenin Blanc/Shiraz) in economy labels at same price points. |
| EU FTA duty reduction looming; premium pricing power at risk | Small Domestic Premium Winemakers | loser | Med | Sula's scale and brand premium allow it to compete; smaller players may face margin squeeze or consolidation. |
| Hospitality capacity constraints limiting high-margin revenue | Sula Vineyards Limited | beneficiary | High | Aggressive capex into tourism (3x winery spend) and Chandon acquisition directly address this bottleneck. |

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Alco-bev premiumization
themes.need: Alco-bev players ride premium-&-above mix shift, single-malt/gin launches and state-excise/route-to-market dynamics - a pricing-power thesis distinct from staple rural-recovery/GST pull.
themes.driver: Premium-mix up-trading, single-malt/gin launches and state-excise/route-to-market dynamics.

growth_optionality.body: Chandon Estate (19 acres) acquisition pending; Targeting >200 room keys within 1.5 years (vs current 154). New event pavilion (Q3FY27) and amphitheater expansion (Q2FY27). CSD listings expanding from 9 to 14 wines by Q4FY27. Potential entry into spirits/tequila via M&A (no target yet).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Transient disruptions (Telangana route-to-market issue, Karnataka tactical destocking) are now largely behind the company, with demand trends improving across key markets entering FY27
- Own Brands showed a progressive recovery in Q4 FY26 (revenue +7.1% YoY, Own Brands +7% YoY) which management expects to carry into FY27
- Premiumization mix shift continues to be a driver, with Elite & Premium share rising to 78.4% of Own Brands in FY26, led by The Source range
- Wine Tourism is a structural growth driver, powered by double-digit footfall growth, room revenue growth and expanded resort capacity (154 keys after The Haven launch)
- A new retail license policy in Uttar Pradesh is expected to enable significant expansion in retail licenses, supporting another strong year for Sula in UP in FY27
- Expansion of CSD listings (9 to 14) is expected to support stronger CSD sales momentum in the second half of FY27
- A healthy Harvest 2026 (sixth consecutive favourable vintage) combined with enhanced storage capacity is expected to ensure adequate grape availability for FY27
- Shift in grape procurement mix toward wine grapes (~99% vs ~80% last year) reflects a conscious strategy to reduce inventory carryover and working capital consumption going into FY27

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin pressured by 350-400bps (expensive wine grapes used in economy labels due to surplus) + 150bps (prior year one-off). Packing material costs rising (West Asia conflict); Price hikes of 2-3% planned in free-pricing states. Opex reduced 3% YoY via cost controls.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: In FY26, Sula commissioned a new 1 million litre low-cost cellar at its Domaine Dindori unit (Maharashtra), built at 33% lower capex, dedicated to Economy & Popular brands, taking total winery capacity to 19.2 million litres. It also increased bottling capacity at two Maharashtra units (Nashik Winery and ND Wines facility), raising WIPS capture to ~100% in FY26 from ~85% in FY25. On the wine-tourism side, the company launched its 3rd resort, The Haven by Sula (50 keys, near York) in Q3 FY26, taking total room capacity to 154 keys, and commissioned a new tasting room and restaurant expansion at Domaine Sula (near Bengaluru) in January 2026. Management's stated Growth Strategy (FY26-FY29) targets accelerating earnings growth via six pillars: product development (new wine launches), sufficient capacity for growth, expanding market penetration (wider national availability of The Source and RASA, new defence listings, new markets), expanding wine tourism & D2C business, augmenting brand visibility, and strategic M&A. The company has signed a binding agreement to acquire Chandon's 19-acre wine estate in Dindori, Nashik, to expand its wine tourism footprint, with the transaction underway and further details to be shared on completion; it also intends to pursue further strategic investments and acquisitions in wine tourism and the Indian AlcoBev industry. On the ESG side, the company doubled its Battery Energy Storage System capacity to ~2,217 kW (~2 MW) and increased solar-powered irrigation pump capacity by 130 HP to a total of 253 HP, alongside continued solar PV capacity build-out (4,703 kWH installed) at its Maharashtra and Karnataka facilities.

- Wine tourism moat: Nashik campus is described as the most-visited vineyard destination globally (over 4 lakh annual visitors), with a hospitality portfolio of three resorts (154 keys) providing a differentiated, difficult-to-replicate asset base

| Hospitality capacity constraints limiting high-margin revenue | Sula Vineyards Limited | beneficiary | High | Aggressive capex into tourism (3x winery spend) and Chandon acquisition directly address this bottleneck. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Completion of the Chandon Estate purchase in Q1 FY27 and its rebranding to Domaine Rāsā is the deck's headline corporate event, opening the presentation ahead of performance highlights.
- [Geographic mix] Telangana, Haryana, Chandigarh, CSD and Exports delivered strong double-digit growth, while "Karnataka continues to remain soft; expect it to turn a corner in H2 FY27" — and the shortfall in core markets (Maharashtra & Karnataka) is named as a driver of adverse market mix on gross margin.
- [Multi-year trajectory] The FY21-FY26 revenue-from-operations series printed is 418 / 454 / 553 / 609 / 619 / 596 (INR Cr) with a stated 6% CAGR, i.e. FY26 revenue was below FY25; Operating EBITDA over the same span was 61 / 113 / 158 / 176 / 149 / 103 (INR Cr) at margins of 14.6% / 25.0% / 28.5% / 28.9% / 24.1% / 17.3%, and PAT was 3 / 52 / 84 / 93 / 70 / 26 (INR Cr). The FY26 figures show a marked step-down from the FY24 peak.
- [Wine tourism trajectory] Wine tourism revenue series of 18 / 35 / 45 / 55 / 60 / 73 (INR Cr) for FY21-FY26, a stated 32% CAGR — the fastest-growing disclosed line and the only one of the six charted series rising in FY26.
